name: 3D Organon VR Anatomy
description: A comprehensive medical XR platform with detailed 3D anatomy, ultrasound simulation, quizzes, and Medverse multi-user sessions.
educational_uses: Designed for in-depth anatomical exploration, medical imaging practice, and collaborative learning for students and professionals.
notes: Guest mode is free; full features require subscription (approx. €499.50–€999.50/year).

name: Acadicus
description: A VR training platform for healthcare education featuring immersive clinical scenarios, patient simulations, and interactive learning environments.
educational_uses: Used by nursing and medical programs to practice clinical decision-making, patient care, and emergency procedures. Instructors can create and customize scenarios for learners.
content_notes: Medical training scenarios may include realistic clinical content.
notes: Institutional license required; not available as a public Quest Store app. Requires managed distribution via Acadicus partnership.

name: Alcohol and Your Brain: A Rollercoaster Ride Through Your Brain
description: An educational VR experience that takes learners on a rollercoaster-style ride through the human brain to show the effects of alcohol on neural pathways.
educational_uses: Useful for health and biology courses—demonstrates neuroscience concepts and substance impacts in an engaging way.
content_notes: Includes rollercoaster-style motion.
notes: Fast-paced rollercoaster simulation; may trigger motion sickness in sensitive users.

name: Alex and the Jets
description: A physics-based VR sandbox where players design and fly jet-powered aircraft. Build your own planes, test flight performance, and explore creative aerodynamics in a fun and experimental environment.
educational_uses: Promotes STEM learning through hands-on experimentation with physics, aerodynamics, and design principles. Excellent for engineering or science outreach events.
content_notes: Flight and building simulation; includes mild motion intensity.
notes: Free in Early Access; active development with new flight parts and challenges being added regularly.

name: American Heart Association CPR VR
description: A public Meta Quest training app from the American Heart Association that teaches Hands-Only CPR and AED basics through an immersive guided experience.
educational_uses: Useful for introducing CPR awareness and basic emergency response concepts in health science, wellness, or public safety settings. Best treated as an awareness and reinforcement tool rather than full certification training.
content_notes: Medical simulation; realistic CPR procedures and emergency response context.
notes: Free public Quest app from the American Heart Association; supports hand tracking and focuses on Hands-Only CPR plus AED awareness.

name: Among Us VR (now "Among Us 3D")
description: The hit social deduction game reimagined for VR—work together as crewmates to complete tasks, or sabotage and deceive as the Impostor.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational, but supports teamwork, communication, and social interaction skills in a group setting.
content_notes: Cartoon violence; online interactions.
notes: Online multiplayer required; voice chat included.

name: AnatomyXR
description: An immersive 3D human anatomy experience—students can isolate systems, use explode view, and interact via hand tracking or controllers.
educational_uses: Perfect for anatomy classes, medical education, and self-directed learning with highly interactive models.
notes: Free on Quest Store; requires internet; supports hand tracking and controllers.

name: Anne Frank House VR
description: A respectful VR recreation of the Secret Annex where Anne Frank and her family lived in hiding, narrated with historical context.
educational_uses: Supports history and humanities courses by immersing students in an important historical site while learning about WWII, human rights, and tolerance.
content_notes: Covers sensitive WWII subject matter including the Holocaust.
notes: Free on Quest; sensitive historical subject matter; best used with guided classroom discussion.

name: Apollo 11 VR
description: A cinematic VR experience replicating the Apollo 11 mission—ride into orbit, land on the moon, and walk where Neil Armstrong did.
educational_uses: Great for space and history learning—immersive depiction of the first moon landing including real audio and environments.
notes: Linear experience (~1 hr), sitting or standing only.

name: Arkio
description: A VR architectural design and planning tool with real-time collaboration.
educational_uses: Architecture students can model buildings, test layouts, and visualize space in VR.
notes: Hand tracking supported

name: Art Plunge
description: A VR gallery app that allows users to step inside famous works of art, exploring iconic paintings as immersive 3D worlds.
educational_uses: Great for art history and humanities courses—lets students experience classic masterpieces in a new way, sparking discussion about art and culture.
content_notes: Some paintings may include artistic nudity (e.g., classical works).
notes: Short experiences designed around individual famous paintings.

name: Audio Trip
description: A VR rhythm and dance game where players move their bodies to hit notes, catch gems, and dodge barriers to the beat of energetic music.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational, but promotes rhythm, physical activity, and coordination. Can be used for fitness initiatives or student engagement events.
content_notes: Energetic gameplay; requires space for movement.
notes: Paid title; includes fitness mode; similar in appeal to Beat Saber with more dance-oriented gameplay.

name: Autismity
description: A VR simulation that places users in the shoes of an autistic person, recreating sensory overload and communication challenges to build empathy and awareness.
educational_uses: Valuable for teacher training, counseling, and social science programs—helps students and educators better understand neurodiversity.
pricing: Custom license (Individual, 1 headset/8 views: EUR 19; Long-term, 1 headset/12mo: EUR 590; Event, 5 headsets/1 day: EUR 390)
content_notes: Simulated sensory overload; may be uncomfortable for sensitive users.
notes: Paid title; intended as an awareness and empathy-building tool, not a diagnostic resource. Not sold on the Meta Quest Store -- requires the vendor's own "Autismity" companion app plus a direct license purchased from theautismsimulator.com.

name: Awake: ECG
description: An immersive VR learning experience that introduces the basics of electrocardiograms (ECG), heart rhythms, and cardiac monitoring in a medical context.
educational_uses: Excellent for health science courses—teaches ECG fundamentals, helping students visualize cardiac rhythms and interpret monitoring results.
content_notes: Medical education focus; ECG waveform interpretation.
notes: Free on Quest; part of the 'Awake' VR educational series.

name: Awake: Heart
description: An immersive VR journey inside the human heart, exploring its structure, function, and life-sustaining role in the body.
educational_uses: Useful for biology and health science courses—helps students visualize anatomy and understand cardiovascular function in an engaging way.
content_notes: Detailed anatomy visuals.
notes: Free on Quest; part of the 'Awake' VR educational series.

name: Bait!
description: A relaxing VR fishing game set across beautiful lakes and environments. Players catch fish, explore new locations, and enjoy peaceful gameplay perfect for unwinding.
educational_uses: While primarily recreational, it promotes mindfulness and stress relief—useful for student wellness programs or casual lab sessions.
content_notes: Gentle fishing gameplay; no violence or intense action.
notes: Free on Quest; includes Bait! Relax VR for social spaces and mini-games.

name: Beat Saber
description: A fast-paced VR rhythm game where players slash blocks to the beat of music using lightsabers.
educational_uses: While primarily a game, it can be used in student life programs for recreation, rhythm training, and fitness activities in the lab.
content_notes: Fast-paced gameplay; high physical activity.
notes: Highly popular VR title; supports DLC music packs; frequent updates.

name: Blaston
description: A competitive 1v1 VR dueling game where players dodge bullets in slow motion and use strategy, reflexes, and precision to win battles in a tight futuristic arena.
educational_uses: Useful for student engagement, esports events, and demonstrations of reflex-based mechanics. Encourages strategic thinking and coordination.
content_notes: Cartoon-style competitive shooting; online multiplayer.
notes: Paid app; supports online multiplayer and frequent tournaments.

name: Blueplanet VR Explore
description: Volumetric VR travel through remarkable natural and cultural scenes—caves, temples, deserts, and more.
educational_uses: Great for geography, art, architecture, and culture classes—immersive field trips with beautiful high-res environments.
notes: Comfortable; offline; includes 40+ scenes in base app.

name: Bodyswaps - Soft Skills Training
description: AI-powered VR simulations where learners practice communication, interviews, leadership, and empathy scenarios with detailed feedback.
educational_uses: Useful for communications, career prep, and healthcare training—lets students role-play and reflect with personalized AI coaching.
content_notes: Requires microphone for speech practice.
notes: Institutional subscription required; free demo available; internet needed.

name: Color-A-Cube
description: A calming VR art experience where players color and decorate 3D cubes and geometric puzzles, creating vibrant designs in a relaxing environment.
educational_uses: Encourages creativity and mindfulness—ideal for art students exploring spatial color, or as a stress-relief activity in student wellness programs.
content_notes: Coloring and pattern creation; no competitive gameplay.
notes: Free to play; designed for relaxation and light creative interaction.

name: Cosmic XR - Space In Your Room
description: A mixed-reality space atlas that brings the solar system, galaxies, and black holes into your room using natural hand interactions.
educational_uses: Excellent for astronomy and Earth science—demonstrates scale, motion, and planet comparisons in an interactive MR format.
notes: Supports hand tracking and passthrough MR; requires open floor space for in-room exploration.

name: CPR Simulator
description: A VR training simulator designed to teach and practice CPR techniques, including chest compressions and emergency response steps.
educational_uses: Great for health science and first aid training—students can practice CPR skills in a safe VR environment and reinforce life-saving procedures.
content_notes: Training simulation; educational but not certification-level.
notes: Simulated training environment; not a substitute for certified CPR courses.

name: CSIxR
description: An immersive VR training tool for crime scene investigation. Students can explore realistic forensic environments, identify evidence, and practice CSI procedures in a safe virtual space.
educational_uses: Designed for criminal justice and forensic science programs—teaches investigative methods, evidence handling, and critical thinking through experiential learning.
content_notes: Crime scene simulation may include sensitive material.
notes: Not publicly available on the Quest Store. Institutional access may require contacting the university or developer directly. Developed by NJIT (New Jersey Institute of Technology) as a research project for NJIT's own crime-scene-investigation training -- no public store listing or public licensing pathway was found. Recommend confirming with NJIT directly or removing this entry if it cannot actually be acquired.

name: Cubism
description: A minimalist 3D puzzle game where players assemble colorful blocks into complex geometric shapes. Relaxing music and intuitive design make it accessible to all skill levels.
educational_uses: Great for developing spatial reasoning, logic, and problem-solving skills. Can be used in STEM or enrichment settings to challenge critical thinking.
notes: Paid title; simple to learn but challenging to master.

name: Dig VR
description: A VR simulator where players operate a realistic excavator—digging, moving soil, and completing construction tasks.
educational_uses: Great for construction and technical education programs—lets students practice heavy equipment operation in a safe and accessible VR setting.
content_notes: Simulated construction work; seated recommended for comfort.
notes: Paid app; moderate comfort due to vehicle movement; designed to simulate real construction work.

name: DuckOrDie – Fitness Boxing Minigames
description: A fast-paced boxing-inspired arcade workout with multiple short minigames focused on dodging, punching, and reflex training.
educational_uses: Encourages physical activity, coordination, and reaction training. Useful for quick demos, active breaks, and wellness programming rather than formal instruction.
content_notes: Active gameplay with cartoon boxing and exaggerated motion.
notes: Free Early Access mixed-reality fitness game; requires physical movement and open space.

name: Electrician Simulator VR
description: A VR simulation where players take on the role of an electrician—repairing sockets, rewiring circuits, installing devices, and solving real-world electrical problems.
educational_uses: Excellent for career & technical education programs. Helps students understand electrical systems, safety procedures, and hands-on troubleshooting in a safe VR environment.
content_notes: Simulated electrical repair tasks—no real danger.
notes: Paid app; requires careful object interaction; great for trade-skills exploration.

name: Elixir
description: A whimsical VR hand-tracking experience where you become a sorcerer’s apprentice, mix potions, and experiment with magical transformations inside a lively alchemy lab.
educational_uses: Perfect for onboarding new users to VR—demonstrates hand tracking, gesture control, and physics-based interaction through a short, engaging experience.
content_notes: Cartoon fantasy humor and mild magical themes.
notes: Free on Quest; designed by Meta Reality Labs; short demo ideal for first-time VR users.

name: Energy Encyclopedia VR
description: An interactive VR exhibit of global energy systems—explore cross-sections of nuclear, hydro, wind, fusion, and solar power plants.
educational_uses: Ideal for STEM and engineering courses—compare generation methods, safety, and environmental impact in detail.
notes: Free on Quest; consider preloading assets for class use.

name: ENGAGE XR
description: A multi-disciplinary virtual events and education platform for classes, conferences, and interactive sessions.
educational_uses: Useful for remote lectures, guest speakers, virtual classrooms, and cross-departmental projects.
notes: Free with premium tiers for advanced features; enterprise options available.

name: Figmin XR
description: A mixed reality creative app for building, animating, and interacting with 3D art.
educational_uses: Encourages students to blend VR and AR by creating interactive MR projects.
notes: Leverages passthrough MR

name: First Contact
description: The original Oculus Touch tutorial experience featuring a retro-inspired robot guide who walks you through VR interactions in a playful 1980s-style playroom.
educational_uses: An iconic VR onboarding app that teaches object interaction, hand presence, and basic VR mechanics on standalone Quest headsets.
content_notes: Legacy tutorial with retro visuals and robot character.
notes: Free official Quest onboarding experience. Separate from the older Rift-era version and still useful for first-time headset users.

name: First Encounters
description: A playful onboarding experience for Quest 3/3S that introduces mixed reality, passthrough, and controller interactions through a short alien encounter game.
educational_uses: Useful as a first VR/MR experience to onboard new users—teaches core mechanics like passthrough, object interaction, and spatial awareness.
content_notes: Short mixed reality onboarding app; cartoon alien characters.
notes: Pre-installed tutorial app for Quest 3/3S; not a full game but ideal for beginners.

name: First Steps
description: A free onboarding experience for Quest headsets that teaches basic VR mechanics with fun interactive mini-games like dancing with a robot and flying a toy blimp.
educational_uses: Excellent for onboarding new VR users—teaches comfort settings, controller use, object interaction, and spatial awareness in a safe, playful way.
content_notes: Short, lighthearted onboarding experience with cartoon visuals.
notes: Originally bundled with Quest 1 & 2; still available for free in the store library.

name: First Steps for Quest 2
description: A free onboarding experience for Quest headsets that teaches basic VR mechanics with fun interactive mini-games like dancing with a robot and flying a toy blimp.
educational_uses: Excellent for onboarding new VR users—teaches comfort settings, controller use, object interaction, and spatial awareness in a safe, playful way.
content_notes: Short, lighthearted onboarding experience with cartoon visuals.
notes: Free onboarding app for modern Quest headsets; store listing is First Steps for Quest 2.

name: Geo Voyage
description: A mixed reality globe for exploring places—drop pins and transition from MR map into immersive VR views with AI-guided exploration.
educational_uses: Great for geography and social sciences—supports virtual field trips, place-based inquiry, and AI-assisted research prompts.
notes: Requires internet; integrates Google Maps and Meta Spatial SDK features.

name: Gods of Gravity
description: A free VR multiplayer strategy game where players act as gods of gravity, controlling fleets and planets in competitive or cooperative matches.
educational_uses: While primarily a game, it can reinforce concepts like orbital mechanics, resource management, and teamwork in a fun way. Great for student engagement and casual esports.
content_notes: Multiplayer competition; sci-fi space battles.
notes: Free-to-play; supports online multiplayer; designed for quick matches and competitive play.

name: Goliath: Playing with Reality
description: An award-winning VR documentary narrated by Tilda Swinton that tells the story of a man living with schizophrenia, exploring themes of mental health, reality, and recovery through gaming and connection.
educational_uses: Useful for counseling, psychology, and humanities courses—raises awareness about mental health, stigma, and the therapeutic potential of games and community.
content_notes: Covers mental health and schizophrenia; includes sensitive personal testimony.
notes: Free on Quest; companion piece to 'Impulse: Playing with Reality.' Sensitive subject matter.

name: Gorilla Tag
description: A social VR phenomenon where players tag, chase, and climb using only their arms to move. Features casual and competitive modes, parkour maps, and active community spaces.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational but promotes physical activity, coordination, and teamwork—can be used in wellness initiatives or social VR events.
content_notes: Highly active gameplay; online multiplayer with voice chat.
notes: Free-to-play with optional in-app purchases. Requires significant arm movement and open play space.

name: Gravity Sketch
description: A professional 3D design tool for sketching, modeling, and prototyping in VR.
educational_uses: Excellent for design, architecture, and engineering students to collaborate on 3D projects.
notes: Accounts for cloud features

name: Headspace XR: Mindfulness & Meditation
description: An immersive VR wellness app from Headspace offering guided meditations, breathing exercises, focus tools, and playful environments to reduce stress and improve mental well-being.
educational_uses: Supports student success initiatives, wellness programs, and stress management by providing accessible mindfulness practices in VR.
content_notes: Meditation and relaxation themes; may not be suited for all learners.
notes: Subscription required after free trial; designed for seated or standing use.

name: Horizon TV
description: The built-in VR video hub for Quest, featuring immersive 360° films, VR shorts, documentaries, livestreams, and curated media content.
educational_uses: Useful for showing VR films, short documentaries, and immersive video content in class or lab settings. Acts as a central hub for VR video learning resources.
content_notes: Content varies—ranging from PG to mature depending on the channel.
notes: Pre-installed on Quest headsets; free to use; requires internet connection. Note: this appears to be the same underlying Meta app as the "TV" catalogue entry (id: tv) -- both point to meta.com/experiences/tv/1931356740318898. Consider de-duplicating.

name: Human Anatomy VR
description: A comprehensive VR anatomy atlas featuring detailed 3D models, Ant Mode miniaturization, muscle animations, quizzes, and collaborative tools. Trusted in universities worldwide for immersive anatomy education.
educational_uses: Great for personal self-study or classroom instruction. Provides deep anatomical exploration and interactive tools for medical, biology, and healthcare education.
notes: Two versions available — personal edition as a one-time purchase (~$29.99) and institutional edition requiring licensing with additional classroom features.

name: IMMERROCK
description: A mixed-reality guitar trainer that overlays chords, tabs, and practice guidance onto your real instrument with real-time accuracy feedback.
educational_uses: Great for applied music courses—supports practice of chords, scales, and rhythm with structured MR lessons.
content_notes: Standing required; best with guitar strap.
notes: Requires a real guitar; passthrough MR with on-device note detection.

name: IMMERSE - Build Real Language Fluency
description: Live instructor-led language sessions with conversation practice and interactive environments.
educational_uses: Supports conversational fluency, cultural exchange, and role-play activities for language courses.
notes: Subscription required; headset microphone recommended.

name: Immersed
description: A VR productivity workspace with multiple virtual monitors, shared team rooms, and customizable focus spaces.
educational_uses: Great for focused study sessions, research, and remote group work across departments.
notes: Free with optional premium plans; account required.

name: Impulse: Playing with Reality
description: A VR documentary experience that explores the science and philosophy of free will, consciousness, and the human mind, blending cinematic storytelling with interactive elements.
educational_uses: Useful for philosophy, psychology, and media studies courses—sparks discussion about neuroscience, choice, and the nature of human reality.
content_notes: Philosophical/scientific content; abstract concepts.
notes: Free app; short, polished documentary experience.

name: In the Shoes of an Autistic Person
description: An immersive VR experience that simulates the world from the perspective of an autistic person, helping users understand sensory differences and challenges.
educational_uses: Useful for counseling, education, and social science programs—supports empathy training, inclusion awareness, and classroom discussions about neurodiversity.
content_notes: Simulated sensory overload; may be uncomfortable for sensitive users.
notes: Free on Quest; short experience designed for awareness and empathy-building.

name: Into the Scaniverse
description: An immersive VR showcase of photogrammetry-based 3D scans from around the world, allowing users to explore real locations and cultural landmarks up close.
educational_uses: Useful for history, geography, and cultural studies—students can virtually visit scanned heritage sites, landscapes, and objects.
content_notes: Educational cultural content; not a game.
notes: Free app featuring a curated collection of 3D-scanned spaces and artifacts.

name: InViewer
description: A VR utility for viewing 3D content, images, and immersive media in a virtual environment.
educational_uses: Useful for classrooms and projects that involve inspecting 3D objects or visual assets directly in VR.
notes: Supports a wide range of 3D/360° content formats.

name: JFK Memento: The Immersive Documentary
description: An immersive VR documentary exploring November 22, 1963—the JFK assassination—through archival film, photos, and narration.
educational_uses: Valuable for U.S. history and civics—analyze primary sources and reflect on media presentation of historical events.
content_notes: Historical reenactment (no graphic content).
notes: Previously released as “Inside History: The JFK Assassination” (by TARGO).

name: Job Simulator
description: A comedic VR game set in a future where robots simulate human jobs. Players can experience exaggerated versions of office work, cooking, auto repair, and more.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational, but introduces VR newcomers to object interaction, motor skills, and creative problem-solving in a lighthearted way.
content_notes: Cartoon humor and light slapstick.
notes: Great for demos and student engagement; highly interactive; requires some open play space.

name: Kingspray Graffiti
description: A VR graffiti simulator with realistic spray paint effects and urban backdrops.
educational_uses: Lets students explore street art safely while discussing art history, culture, and expression.
notes: Comfort turns for classroom use

name: Labster VR
description: A VR science education platform providing hundreds of virtual labs across biology, chemistry, physics, and more. Students can conduct experiments in safe, immersive environments.
educational_uses: Designed for high schools and universities to give students hands-on lab experience without material costs or safety risks. Labs integrate with LMS platforms and provide guided lessons with assessments.
content_notes: Covers scientific experiments and lab procedures.
notes: Requires institutional license; not publicly available on the Quest Store. Used widely in schools and higher education. Labster's simulations are primarily browser/desktop-based (LMS-integrated), not a native standalone Quest headset app in the traditional sense -- verify fit before counting it as "installed" XR Lab hardware content.

name: Liminal
description: A collection of short VR experiences grounded in neuroscience and psychology, designed to quickly change your emotional and mental state.
educational_uses: Supports wellness initiatives—can be used in counseling or student success programs to promote relaxation, focus, or energy boosts through guided VR experiences.
content_notes: Mood-altering experiences—designed for short sessions.
notes: Free with optional subscription for more content; experiences are 2–10 minutes long.

name: Match Point Tennis
description: A realistic tennis simulator featuring precise racket physics, AI opponents, and online multiplayer. Players can participate in career mode or quick matches, training their timing and coordination.
educational_uses: Encourages physical activity and coordination while introducing competitive play and sportsmanship. Great for fitness programs, esports clubs, or active lab sessions.
content_notes: Active gameplay requiring full arm movement.
notes: Paid title; offers both single-player tournaments and online multiplayer. More structured and simulation-focused than Tennis Esports.

name: Meta for Education (MDM / Admin Center)
description: Meta discontinued the paid "Meta Quest for Business"/"Meta Quest for Education" hardware+license bundle as of February 20, 2026. In its place, Horizon Managed Services (HMS) -- the actual device-management/MDM layer -- is now free to register at meta.com/meta-for-work and works with ordinary consumer Quest 3/3S hardware. HMS/MDM is only needed for centralized fleet management (remote config, kiosk mode, security policies, silent app deployment); it is not required just to install and use a normally purchased app.
educational_uses: Required by some education apps. Lets IT centrally configure headsets so teachers can start class quickly without per-device setup.
content_notes: Service (not an in-headset app).
notes: Integrates with enterprise MDMs (e.g., Intune, VMware Workspace ONE). Licensing is subscription-based. Check MHMS policies if you need Meta Store access on managed devices. Program history: previously a paid Meta Quest for Business/Education bundle; discontinued Feb 20, 2026 in favor of free HMS registration usable with consumer hardware.

name: Meta Horizon Worlds
description: Meta’s social VR platform where users can explore immersive worlds, attend events, and build their own interactive experiences with creation tools.
educational_uses: Useful for exploring virtual collaboration, game design, and social interaction. Can be leveraged for student clubs, creative projects, and experimenting with immersive media.
content_notes: Online social interactions; user-generated content may vary. Meta announced a full VR shutdown of Horizon Worlds (effective June 15, 2026) and removed it from the Quest Store by March 31, 2026, then partially reversed course: existing worlds remain playable in VR, but new-world creation is now mobile/web-only. Verify current relevance before recommending.
notes: Free to download; requires a Meta account; as of March 19, 2026, Meta kept VR support active, but mobile is now the primary focus.

name: Meta Quest Help & Tips
description: The built-in Meta Quest help center with setup guides, safety tips, and troubleshooting resources for new users.
educational_uses: Useful for onboarding lab participants—provides official Meta instructions for safety, controller use, Guardian setup, and VR best practices.
content_notes: Covers VR safety and usage guidelines.
notes: Pre-installed on Quest devices; free; accessible anytime from the app library.

name: Mission: ISS
description: An immersive simulation of life aboard the International Space Station—learn to dock, spacewalk, and explore using real NASA models and astronaut-led media.
educational_uses: Strong STEM content—ideal for learning about space, robotics, physics, and astronaut workflows.
notes: Free non-profit experience; Emmy-nominated.

name: MLK: Now is the Time
description: An immersive VR interpretation of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s “I Have a Dream” speech, blending historic audio with present-day perspectives.
educational_uses: Useful for civil rights and U.S. history courses—connects 1963 to today, prompting reflection and discussion on equity.
content_notes: Includes sensitive social issues (racism, inequality).
notes: Free on Quest; includes sensitive social topics—plan guided debriefing.

name: Mondly: Learn Languages in VR
description: A VR language learning app with conversational practice, speech recognition, and immersive scenarios.
educational_uses: Supports ESL and world languages by giving students an interactive way to practice speaking and listening in context.
notes: Free to download; subscription required for full lessons; headset microphone needed.

name: Nano
description: An immersive VR science experience that shrinks you down to explore the nanoscale world of molecules, atoms, and cutting-edge nanotechnology.
educational_uses: Useful for science and STEM classes to introduce concepts of nanotechnology, molecular structures, and their applications in medicine and engineering.
notes: Short, cinematic VR journey; designed as an educational showcase.

name: Nanome
description: A VR interface for visualizing, building, and simulating molecular structures like DNA, proteins, and more.
educational_uses: Excellent for chemistry and biology education, enabling interactive molecular exploration and simulation.
notes: Free basic version; premium features via paid licenses

name: Notes on Blindness
description: A VR documentary based on the audio diaries of John Hull, exploring the experience of blindness through sound-rich, abstract environments.
educational_uses: Supports discussions in disability studies, empathy building, and humanities by immersing students in sensory storytelling.
content_notes: Themes of disability and personal reflection.
notes: Audio-heavy experience; best used with quality headphones.

name: Noun Town: Language Learning
description: A gamified VR language learning platform where learners practice vocabulary and phrases in an interactive virtual town.
educational_uses: Supports ESL and world languages by engaging students in active practice through contextual VR settings.
notes: Paid app; offers multiple languages; supports gamified learning.

name: Novo Nordisk Heritage Experience
description: An immersive educational VR experience that guides users through the history of insulin discovery, diabetes treatment, and the innovations of Novo Nordisk. Combines storytelling, interactive exhibits, and scientific insights.
educational_uses: Ideal for health science and biology education—illustrates medical breakthroughs and the evolution of diabetes care. Also valuable for history and ethics discussions around scientific innovation.
content_notes: Historical medical themes and scientific context.
notes: Free Quest experience produced by Novo Nordisk; museum-style narrative with interactive elements and hand-tracking support.

name: Ocean Rift
description: A peaceful underwater journey exploring marine environments—swim with sharks, dolphins, and prehistoric creatures.
educational_uses: Ideal for biology and marine science—experience diverse ocean ecosystems in VR rich with detail.
notes: Comfortable experience; mixed-reality support on compatible headsets; often on sale (~$6).

name: On The Morning You Wake (To the End of the World)
description: An award-winning VR documentary that immerses viewers in the events of the 2018 Hawaii ballistic missile false alert. Through powerful narration and visuals, it explores how misinformation and fear affect individuals and communities.
educational_uses: Excellent for courses in media literacy, communications, and social psychology. Encourages discussion on crisis response, misinformation, and resilience in the digital age.
content_notes: Depicts real-world fear and crisis response; emotionally intense subject matter.
notes: Free on Quest; emotionally intense but non-graphic; developed by Atlas V, Astrea, and Archer’s Mark.

name: Open Blocks
description: A creative VR sandbox where users can build, experiment, and explore the laws of physics. Construct complex machines, test interactions, and learn engineering logic through hands-on play.
educational_uses: Excellent for STEM and engineering education—encourages problem-solving, systems thinking, and experimentation with real-time physics in a virtual lab.
content_notes: Sandbox creation with building and physics experimentation.
notes: Free in Early Access; designed for creators, educators, and tinkerers. Features physics simulation and block-based construction.

name: Open Brush
description: An open-source continuation of Google’s Tilt Brush, allowing 3D brush strokes in space.
educational_uses: Useful for teaching spatial art, VR creativity, and immersive design projects.
notes: Community-supported fork of Tilt Brush

name: Orion Drift
description: A social sci-fi movement game from Another Axiom where players run, jump, climb, skate, and fly through large space-station hubs with dozens of other players.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational, but useful for exploring multiplayer VR movement, spatial awareness, and social interaction in a futuristic setting. Better fit for student life or social VR demos than formal STEM instruction.
content_notes: Online multiplayer social play with fast physical movement in a sci-fi setting.
notes: Free-to-play Early Access title with online multiplayer and large shared social spaces.

name: Ovation
description: A VR public speaking trainer where you present to realistic AI audiences and receive detailed feedback on delivery.
educational_uses: Excellent for speech, communications, and business courses—practice interviews, presentations, and Q&A in realistic settings.
notes: Headset mic recommended; subscription features available.

name: Painting VR
description: A hands-on VR painting workshop with large-scale canvases and customizable tools.
educational_uses: Allows students to practice painting techniques without materials or mess.
notes: Room-scale recommended

name: Paradiddle
description: A VR drumming simulator that lets you play realistic drum kits using VR controllers or connect a MIDI drum kit for advanced practice. Features custom kit building, recording, and practice tools.
educational_uses: Great for music programs—students can practice drumming techniques, rhythm, and timing in VR, with or without access to physical drums.
content_notes: Requires space for drumming gestures; optional MIDI device support.
notes: Supports MIDI device integration; paid app with strong music education potential.

name: PianoVision
description: A mixed reality piano learning app that overlays falling notes and practice guidance onto a real or virtual keyboard. Includes tutorials, sheet music import, and practice modes.
educational_uses: Great for music programs and self-paced learning—students can practice piano with real-time feedback in VR/MR, using either a physical keyboard or virtual keys.
content_notes: Works best with a physical piano/keyboard.
notes: Free to try; subscription unlocks full lessons and advanced features. Best used with a real MIDI keyboard.

name: Puzzling Places
description: A relaxing and meditative 3D jigsaw puzzle game where players assemble highly detailed models of real-world places captured with photogrammetry.
educational_uses: Excellent for developing spatial reasoning, focus, and problem-solving skills. Also highlights cultural heritage sites through immersive puzzles.
content_notes: Relaxing gameplay; suitable for all ages.
notes: Paid app with DLC puzzle packs available; highly recommended for enrichment and logic-based learning.

name: Quill by Smoothstep
description: A professional VR painting and animation tool originally developed by Oculus Story Studio, now maintained by Smoothstep. Enables artists to create immersive illustrations and full animated short films in VR.
educational_uses: Excellent for advanced media arts and animation programs—teaches VR-native creative workflows, narrative development, and immersive visual design.
content_notes: Creation software; requires external PC hardware.
notes: Free on PCVR; requires a VR-ready computer with Quest Link or Air Link. Not a standalone Quest app. This is a PCVR (Rift/PC-headset) store listing, not a standalone Quest listing -- using it may require a PC plus Quest Link/Air Link rather than working standalone on a headset.

name: Rome
description: A cinematic VR journey that explores the history and architecture of ancient Rome through immersive visuals and narration.
educational_uses: Useful for history and classics courses—introduces Roman culture, architecture, and storytelling through cinematic VR.
notes: Short linear VR film experience; best suited for classroom demonstrations.

name: SAIL
description: An open-world VR pirate adventure where players captain their own ship, explore islands, hunt for treasure, and engage in physics-based naval combat and sailing mechanics.
educational_uses: While primarily recreational, it reinforces principles of physics, navigation, and resource management—great for experiential learning or themed lab events.
pricing: Paid (EUR 29.99) -- left Early Access Jan 2026, was previously free
content_notes: Cartoon-style ship combat and treasure hunting; mild motion intensity.
notes: Free multiplayer pirate adventure; includes locomotion and ship motion, so comfort settings may help new VR users.

name: SculptrVR
description: A beginner-friendly VR sculpting and voxel modeling tool for creating 3D objects.
educational_uses: Good for introducing students to 3D design, modeling concepts, and creative prototyping.
notes: Beginner-friendly

name: ShapesXR
description: A collaborative VR prototyping tool for UI/UX and spatial design.
educational_uses: Useful in computer science and design programs for testing user interfaces and team collaboration.
notes: Great for team reviews

name: Sharecare YOU: Anatomy
description: A detailed human anatomy explorer with layered systems and guided lessons.
educational_uses: Great for anatomy and physiology to examine organs, systems, and clinical context in 3D.
notes: Standalone app

name: Spatial
description: A social VR platform for exhibits, galleries, and community events.
educational_uses: Students and faculty can host showcases, poster sessions, and interactive cultural spaces.
notes: Requires free account; supports multiplayer collaboration.

name: Synth Riders
description: A VR rhythm game where players ride the rails of music, hit notes with freestyle dance-inspired movements, and enjoy a diverse soundtrack with DLC packs.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational, but supports rhythm training, coordination, and physical activity. Great for student events, esports-style competitions, or wellness initiatives.
content_notes: Energetic gameplay; requires room for movement.
notes: Base game is paid; DLC music packs available. Strong multiplayer and fitness community support. Also included in the Meta Quest+ subscription catalog as of this audit, in addition to standalone purchase.

name: Tablecraft
description: A VR science-crafting sandbox where you combine atomic blocks to discover new elements, isotopes, and over 900 possible recipes. Experiment with radioactive decay, fission, and elemental reactions to unlock the entire periodic table.
educational_uses: Excellent for chemistry and physics programs—gamifies atomic structure, isotopes, and nuclear reactions in an accessible and humorous way. Encourages experimentation and scientific curiosity.
content_notes: Cartoon science humor; includes radiation and chemistry references.
notes: Currently free in Early Access. Combines science concepts with creative crafting gameplay in a lighthearted lab setting.

name: Tennis Esports: Fun, Social, Competitive
description: A realistic VR tennis simulation featuring physics-based ball mechanics, online multiplayer, and professional training options. Players can practice swings, play matches, or compete in global tournaments.
educational_uses: Supports physical education, wellness, and esports programs—improves coordination, cardio, and competitive sports engagement in a safe, virtual setting.
content_notes: Physical activity; may require large play area.
notes: Currently free in Early Access; offers single-player practice and online multiplayer. Requires open play area for safe movement.

name: The Body VR: Journey Inside a Cell
description: Travel through the bloodstream and enter a living cell to explore its organelles and functions.
educational_uses: Helps students visualize cell biology, organelle functions, and human anatomy at the microscopic level.
notes: Short, immersive experience (under 30 minutes); moderate comfort level.

name: The Hydrous Presents: EXPLORE
description: An immersive underwater VR journey created by The Hydrous, designed to teach ocean science and highlight conservation efforts through guided exploration of coral reefs and marine ecosystems.
educational_uses: Excellent for natural science and environmental studies—lets students experience marine biodiversity and learn about conservation challenges firsthand.
content_notes: Ocean environments; includes conservation messaging.
notes: Free on Quest; produced by ocean scientists and conservationists; best with headphones for narration and sound design.

name: Theater, Elsewhere
description: The official VR showcase for immersive stories and animations created with Quill. Theater, Elsewhere hosts a collection of narrative VR shorts and experimental art pieces.
educational_uses: Valuable for media arts, digital storytelling, and animation education—demonstrates how VR can be used as a medium for narrative and artistic expression.
content_notes: VR art and storytelling content; experimental narrative works.
notes: Successor to Quill Theater; free to access on Quest Store.

name: Titanic VR
description: Explore the wreck of the RMS Titanic through immersive dives, ROV missions, and cinematic historical sequences.
educational_uses: Great for discussing evidence collection, maritime history, and ethics of preservation through interactive exploration.
content_notes: Disaster theme may be distressing for some learners.
notes: Single-player; includes story content and free exploration missions (~6+ hours total).

name: Titans of Space PLUS
description: A guided, scale-accurate VR tour through the solar system and nearby stars with voice narration, interactive stops, and comfort settings.
educational_uses: Perfect for teaching astronomy and spatial reasoning—includes basic and extended tours, planetary comparisons, and gravity probes.
notes: Comfortable motion mode; optional short (~20 min) or long (~35 min) tour; well-rated by educators.

name: TRANSFR VR
description: A VR training platform focused on career and technical education, offering hands-on simulations for trades, safety, and job skills. Used in schools, workforce programs, and community colleges.
educational_uses: Provides immersive training scenarios for industries such as manufacturing, automotive, construction, and hospitality. Helps students and job seekers gain practical experience and career readiness.
pricing: Institutional license (subscription, contact Transfr for pricing)
content_notes: Job training scenarios; some modules may include simulated workplace hazards.
notes: Institutional license required; distributed directly to schools and training centers, not available on the public Quest Store.

name: TRIPP
description: Guided mindfulness and meditation experiences with calming visuals, music, and breathwork prompts.
educational_uses: Supports student well-being, stress management, and mental health initiatives on campus.
content_notes: Visual patterns may be intense for sensitive users.
notes: Subscription required after free trial; seated recommended.

name: TV
description: Meta's built-in video and streaming hub for Quest, featuring immersive 180° and 360° films alongside flat-screen streaming content in VR and mixed reality.
educational_uses: Useful for showing immersive films, short documentaries, and curated VR video content in class or lab settings. Also works as a simple media hub for headset-based viewing.
content_notes: Content varies—ranging from PG to mature depending on the channel.
notes: Pre-installed on Quest headsets; free to use; renamed to TV in 2025 after previously being called Meta Quest TV. Note: this appears to be the same underlying Meta app as the "Horizon TV" catalogue entry (id: horizon-tv) -- both point to meta.com/experiences/tv/1931356740318898. Consider de-duplicating.

name: Vermillion
description: A realistic VR oil painting studio with tools, color mixing, and lifelike canvas textures.
educational_uses: Great for art classes to explore painting techniques, color theory, and digital studio practice.
content_notes: Pricing could not be confirmed this pass (store listing found, but price not verified) -- left as "Unknown" rather than guessed.
notes: Controllers recommended

name: VictoryXR
description: A comprehensive VR education platform providing a wide range of immersive modules including virtual dissection labs, science demonstrations, history field trips, and full VictoryXR Campus experiences.
educational_uses: Covers multiple subjects across STEM, humanities, and career education. Enables virtual classrooms, lab simulations, and collaborative campus environments designed for schools and universities.
pricing: Institutional license / subscription (contact VictoryXR for pricing)
content_notes: Content varies by subject—includes science dissections, history reenactments, and more.
notes: Institutional license required; not a standalone public app. VictoryXR partners with schools to deploy customized VR curricula. Licensing model: "licenses follow the student, not the device" -- runs on most major VR headsets plus Windows/Mac. Also offers a turnkey "$47,000 Classroom Simulation Lab" bundle (25 Quest headsets + software + charging cart + onsite training).

name: Walkabout Mini Golf
description: A VR mini-golf game with realistic physics, beautiful themed courses, and fun multiplayer support. Includes hidden collectibles and expansion DLC courses.
educational_uses: Primarily recreational, but promotes social interaction, teamwork, and fine motor coordination. Great for student engagement events.
content_notes: Mild competitive elements; online interactions.
notes: Paid base game with optional DLC courses; supports online multiplayer.

name: Wander
description: A VR world explorer powered by Street View imagery—visit landmarks and locations from around the globe.
educational_uses: Great for virtual field trips, geography lessons, and cultural studies, enabling place-based learning in the classroom.
notes: Requires internet connection; Street View-style navigation.

name: Warship Mars
description: Dive to the 1564 wreck of the Swedish warship Mars, recreated with photogrammetry. Explore underwater, document finds, and analyze artifacts in a virtual research space.
educational_uses: Excellent for history and archaeology units—virtual fieldwork, evidence collection, and discussions on maritime technology and preservation.
content_notes: Underwater diving may cause discomfort for some users.
notes: Free on Quest; includes Diving and Researcher modes.

name: We Live Here
description: An immersive VR documentary that shares the stories of unhoused individuals, providing insight into housing inequality and social challenges.
educational_uses: Useful for social sciences, counseling, and humanities—supports empathy training and discussions on systemic inequality, poverty, and housing justice.
content_notes: Addresses homelessness and systemic inequality; sensitive themes.
notes: Free VR documentary experience; short runtime; sensitive subject matter.

name: Wooorld
description: A mixed reality 3D world map with real-world terrain, cities, and multiplayer exploration.
educational_uses: Great for virtual field trips, cultural geography, and group learning in MR—students can explore cities, landmarks, and natural features together.
notes: Requires internet; supports multiplayer sessions.

name: Prisms Math
description: A K-12 math curriculum delivered in VR, immersing students in interactive real-world problems to build conceptual understanding in middle-school math, Algebra I, and Geometry (fractions, ratios, linear functions, systems of equations, quadratics, transformations, trig ratios, and more).
educational_uses: Built for grades 8-11 math classes; includes single-player content modules, a multiplayer practice sandbox, and a web dashboard for teachers to monitor progress and give feedback.
notes: Verify current per-seat/classroom pricing directly with Prisms before purchasing for a full class.

name: The VR Chemistry Lab
description: A hands-on chemistry lab in VR where students build molecules, run chemical reactions, and explore concepts in an immersive environment. Originally built as a VR-learning research tool, now used for classroom and at-home chemistry practice.
educational_uses: Lets students safely run experiments and build/molecule visualizations that would be impractical or unsafe in a physical classroom lab.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: National Geographic Explore VR
description: Travel as a National Geographic explorer to Antarctica and Machu Picchu -- kayak among icebergs, climb ice shelves, and explore a digital reconstruction of the ancient Inca citadel, with background/educational narration throughout.
educational_uses: Pairs well with the existing 360 travel/geography content (Wander, Wooorld, Geo Voyage) but adds Nat Geo's editorial/documentary layer and stronger narrative framing.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: Paleontology VR
description: Step into the role of a paleontologist: dig for fossils in the field, clean and restore them in a lab using real tools, then assemble complete dinosaur skeletons to display in your own virtual museum.
educational_uses: Hands-on introduction to fossil excavation and preparation methodology; good fit for earth science or biology units on prehistoric life.
pricing: Unknown -- price not confirmed, verify on store page before purchasing
notes: Developed by Rambutan Dog Games; includes multiplayer/party modes in addition to the solo excavation content.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: Silent Classroom: ASL VR
description: An American Sign Language practice app set in a virtual ASL classroom, using hand tracking so students can sign the alphabet and practice finger spelling, with a narrative thread covering ASL history and figures like Irving King Jordan.
educational_uses: The only sign-language-focused title in the catalogue -- useful for ASL courses, disability-awareness units, or general accessibility education. Hand tracking is required (no controllers).
pricing: Unknown -- price not confirmed, verify on store page before purchasing
notes: Requires hand tracking, not controllers -- confirm classroom headsets support it well before relying on this for a lesson.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: Pencil - Learn to Draw
description: An award-winning mixed-reality drawing tutor: it overlays digital guide lines onto real paper (viewed through Quest 3/3S passthrough) so you draw with an actual pencil while following step-by-step lessons. 80+ lessons cover basics through construction, perspective, and shading, guided by an on-desk animated teacher.
educational_uses: A structured, tutorial-driven complement to the catalogue's free-drawing/painting apps (Open Brush, Vermillion, Painting VR) -- teaches drawing fundamentals rather than just providing a canvas.
notes: Requires Quest 3 or 3S passthrough plus real paper and a pencil -- will not work on Quest 2/Pro.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: ArtQuest VR - Hundreds of Museums
description: A virtual art museum with works from hundreds of real collections (MoMA, the Uffizi Galleries, the Rijksmuseum, and more) -- browse by artist, movement, or museum, view pieces at true scale, zoom in for detail, and read museum-style labels with optional audio narration.
educational_uses: A strong virtual-field-trip option for art history, humanities, or cultural studies classes -- pairs with the catalogue's Louvre and museum-tour WebXR content but adds a much larger, browsable multi-museum collection.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: FitXR
description: A VR fitness platform with instructor-led Box, Combat, HIIT, Dance, Flow, and Sculpt classes set to music, run in quarterly seasons with new content added regularly.
educational_uses: Good fit for kinesiology/PE-adjacent programs or general wellness programming -- full-body cardio and strength workouts with real-time feedback on form/intensity.
content_notes: Vigorous full-body exercise; needs clear play space.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: Innerworld by XRHealth
description: A virtual peer-support space where users learn evidence-based mental health tools -- including Cognitive Behavioral Immersion -- guided by certified guides, working through anxiety, stress, and other challenges in a group setting.
educational_uses: Complements the catalogue's individual meditation/mindfulness apps (Tripp, Liminal, Headspace XR) with a peer-support and certified-guide model -- worth reviewing with counseling staff before recommending to students, since it involves real people and group sessions rather than solo content.
pricing: Unknown -- appears to combine free access with a support/clinical component; verify current model directly
content_notes: Involves live group interaction with other users and certified guides, not a solo/offline experience -- review privacy and appropriateness for a school setting before use.
notes: Currently for English speakers only, per the publisher.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: SimX VR
description: A professional-grade, wireless, multiplayer VR medical training simulation letting physicians, nurses, and allied health professionals practice on virtual patients in configurable clinical environments. Designed by physicians at Stanford and UCSF; used at medical and nursing schools nationally.
educational_uses: Aimed at health science / nursing / EMT programs wanting realistic multiplayer clinical scenario training rather than static anatomy content -- complements 3D Organon and Human Anatomy VR.
notes: Designed for institutional/program adoption, not an individual consumer purchase.

_source.added: 2026-07-20 catalogue expansion (art/fitness/wellness/mental health/medical + prior science/art-history round)

name: VR Nurse Sim by Simlogic
description: A nursing-skills simulator for junior healthcare professionals, developed with a Norwegian vocational institution. Multiple scenarios in clinical and home settings train ABCDE patient assessment, the NEWS2 early-warning score, and ISBAR clinical communication.
educational_uses: A more structured, curriculum-aligned complement to SimX -- good fit for entry-level nursing or CNA/health-science programs focused on foundational assessment and communication protocols.
notes: Also listed under the title "Skillup VR NurseSIM" -- same underlying app/ID.
